task.title: Fix Source Ingestion durable terminal readback gap

root_cause.summary: The source-ingestion write and readback code path (services/source_ingestion/main.py, configured.py, scheduler.py) works correctly and needed no product code change. The deployed E2E boundary failed for two independent reasons in the test harness itself, both proven by direct reproduction against the live pantheon compose stack (source-ingest on 127.0.0.1:18097).
candidates_ruled_out: scheduler.run_once idempotency: run_once completed normally on every attempt (run.status == completed, raw_count == normalized_count == 1); no retry or duplicate-run defect observed.

configured fetch batch persistence: ConfiguredConnectorFetcher.fetch_batch correctly returned the static_records payload every time (connector fetch state showed successful_attempts == attempts, 0 failures).
root_cause.confirmed_cause: A store identity mismatch between write and read paths, entirely inside the test harness (tests/integration/l12/test_current_research_loops_deployed_e2e.py), with two independent contributing defects: (1) GET /api/source-ingest/source-records/{source_id} returns the established envelope {"source_record": {...}} (matching tests/e2e/test_source_to_strategy_spec.py and every other source-ingest read endpoint's {"item"|"bundle"|"connector"} shape), but the poll accept-predicate compared value.get("source_id") on the un-unwrapped envelope, so it could never match even once the record existed, and the harness would time out. (2) Once (1) is fixed, a second, environment-triggered mismatch surfaces on any pantheon compose project that has run this suite before: the test's static_records payload used a fixed, non-unique metadata.body string across every run. services/knowledge/evidence/normalization.py content-addresses SourceRecords by content_hash (derived from metadata.body) when no canonical_doi/repo/url is present, and services/source_ingestion/main.py::_persist_source_evidence_refs correctly honors that existing dedupe owner. On a fresh store the newly generated source_id is its own dedupe owner and readback succeeds; on a reused store (the deployed E2E's own target) the fixed body text collides with a prior run's SourceRecord, so the new job's post-processing legitimately attaches evidence to the old owner id and the freshly generated source_id is deliberately never assigned its own record. The caller-declared source_id therefore never resolves, independent of any correctness bug in the ingestion pipeline itself.
reproduction: In-process FastAPI TestClient run (jsonl evidence backend, single process): POST /api/source-ingest/connectors -> 201, PUT .../schedule -> 200, POST /api/source-ingest/jobs (connector_id only, no records field) -> 201 with run.status=completed, GET /api/source-ingest/source-records/{source_id} -> 200 with the exact posted source_id, proving the production write/read path is correct end to end.

Live deployed pantheon compose stack (source-ingest on 127.0.0.1:18097, SOURCE_INGEST_EVIDENCE_BACKEND=postgres): first run against the long-lived shared environment passed source.durable_terminal_readback; a second run with the original static body text reproduced a persistent 404 even though GET /api/source-ingest/jobs showed the ingest run completed with normalized_count=1, confirming the dedupe-owner redirection rather than a lost write.

changes: Added DeployedResearchHarness._source_record(view), matching the existing _entry(view) unwrap-helper pattern already used for the strategy-spec registry boundary, and used it to unwrap the {"source_record": ...} envelope before comparing source_id in the durable_terminal_readback poll accept-predicate and before computing _source_digest(source).

Made the static_records connector payload's metadata.body include self.run_token so each E2E run produces a distinct content_hash / source_dedupe_key and cannot collide with a prior run's SourceRecord on a reused compose deployment. The POST call sequence (connector configure -> schedule -> job trigger -> readback poll -> controller readback) is unchanged; only the read-side parsing and the per-run content value changed.
fix.not_changing: services/source_ingestion/main.py, services/source_ingestion/configured.py, services/source_ingestion/scheduler.py, and services/knowledge/evidence/normalization.py are unmodified; the content-addressed dedupe design in normalization.py is intentional product behavior for genuinely duplicate content and is left in place.
fix.owned_layer: Deployed E2E harness readback parsing and per-run content uniqueness for the source_ingestion identity-chain case.
